keyAndScale.primaryKey: F# minor (sounding key with capo 2; played as Em shapes)

scalesUsed.notes: F# - G# - A - B - C# - D - E - F#
scalesUsed.application: Overall harmonic framework; all chords derive from this key center

scalesUsed.notes: E - F# - G - A - B - C - D - E
scalesUsed.application: The chord shapes and fingerings used with capo 2 correspond to E minor open position chords

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Aeolian (Natural Minor) with suspended chord color
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: F# minor is the relative minor of A major

mainProgression.description: Signature Wonderwall progression using suspended chord voicings that create the dreamy, unresolved character of the song. Played with capo 2, sounding as F#m7 - A - Esus4 - B7sus4.

sectionProgressions.description: Repeating four-chord loop with sustained strumming pattern that drives the verse melody forward
Transitional passage that builds tension with the C major chord before resolving back to the tonic
The iconic 'because maybe' section with a sing-along melody anchored by the Em7 tonic resolution

harmonicFunction: Em7 (i7) - Tonic minor seventh chord providing the melancholy home base
G (III) - Major mediant chord adding brightness and lift to the minor key
Dsus4 (VII sus4) - Subtonic chord with suspended fourth creating yearning, unresolved quality
A7sus4 (IV7 sus4) - Subdominant seventh with suspension adding tension before resolution
C (V in relative sense) - Provides harmonic contrast in pre-chorus sections

techniques.name: Suspended Chord Strumming Pattern
techniques.description: The signature Wonderwall strumming pattern using a syncopated down-down-up-up-down-up rhythm that gives the song its distinctive driving feel

notes: Em7: 0-2-2-0-3-3 (keep ring and pinky fingers anchored on 3rd fret B and high E strings)
G: 3-2-0-0-3-3 (same anchored fingers on top two strings)
Dsus4: X-X-0-2-3-3 (anchored fingers maintain continuity)
A7sus4: X-0-2-0-3-3 (anchored fingers create the suspended sound)
C: X-3-2-0-1-0 (standard C shape for pre-chorus)
The anchored ring and pinky fingers on the 3rd fret of B and high E strings are the key to the Wonderwall sound
All shapes played relative to capo 2 position
sequence: Anchor ring finger on 3rd fret B string and pinky on 3rd fret high E string
Play the strumming pattern: Down - Down - Up - Up - Down - Up
Maintain anchored fingers while changing chord shapes underneath
Keep the strumming hand moving in constant 16th-note motion
tips: Keep your strumming hand moving even when not striking strings (ghost strums)
The anchored fingers on the top two strings are essential - they create the signature sound
Practice the pattern slowly with a metronome before adding chord changes
Let the strings ring out - avoid palm muting

techniques.name: Capo Chord Shapes
techniques.description: Using a capo on the 2nd fret to play simple open chord shapes that sound in a higher key, a fundamental acoustic guitar technique

notes: Capo 2 transposes all open chord shapes up one whole step
Em7 shape sounds as F#m7
G shape sounds as A major
Dsus4 shape sounds as Esus4
A7sus4 shape sounds as B7sus4
C shape sounds as D major
This allows playing in F# minor using simple open position shapes
sequence: Attach capo firmly on 2nd fret, close to the fret wire
Check tuning after applying capo (it can pull strings sharp)
Play chord shapes as if the capo were the nut
Fret numbers are relative to capo position
tips: Place the capo as close to the 2nd fret wire as possible for clean tone
Re-tune after placing the capo - spring tension can detune strings slightly
Apply even pressure across all strings
A quality capo makes a big difference in tone and tuning stability
details.progression: Em7 - G - Dsus4 - A7sus4 transposed by capo 2

techniques.name: Anchored Finger Technique
techniques.description: Keeping the ring and pinky fingers stationary on the 3rd fret of the B and high E strings while changing chord shapes underneath, creating the characteristic suspended chord embellishments

notes: Ring finger stays on 3rd fret of B string throughout
Pinky finger stays on 3rd fret of high E string throughout
Only the index and middle fingers move to change chords
This creates the suspended and seventh chord voicings naturally
The technique simplifies chord changes dramatically
sequence: Place ring finger on 3rd fret B string
Place pinky on 3rd fret high E string
Form Em7 with remaining fingers (index on 2nd fret A string)
Move to G by adding middle finger to 3rd fret low E string
Shift to Dsus4 by moving to 2nd fret G string
Change to A7sus4 with 2nd fret D string
tips: Practice keeping the top two fingers absolutely still during changes
This is the secret to smooth, fast chord transitions in this song
Build finger independence by practicing the anchor while moving other fingers
The anchored notes are what give Wonderwall its signature jangly sound
details.progression: All verse and chorus chord shapes with anchored fingers

sections.name: Intro / Verse
sections.description: The iconic opening strumming pattern establishing the song's dreamy atmosphere with the four-chord loop
notes: Strumming pattern: Down-Down-Up-Up-Down-Up in 16th-note feel
Keep ring and pinky fingers anchored on 3rd fret of B and high E strings
Let all strings ring openly for maximum sustain
Maintain steady tempo at 87 BPM throughout

sections.name: Pre-Chorus
sections.description: Building section with the C and Dsus4 chords creating harmonic tension before the chorus release
notes: Slightly increased strumming intensity to build energy
The C chord breaks the anchored finger pattern briefly
Quick transition back to Em7 at the end of the section
Vocal melody rises to build anticipation for chorus

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: The signature 'Because maybe, youthe signature section with powerful sing-along energy
notes: Full strumming intensity for maximum impact
Emphasize downstrokes on beat 1 of each chord change
The Em7 resolution gives the chorus its emotional weight
Repeat the chorus progression twice before returning to verse

sections.name: Outro
sections.description: Extended chorus repetition with gradual dynamic build, incorporating layered guitar textures in the original recording
notes: Repeated chorus progression with building intensity
Original recording adds lead guitar melody over strumming
Maintain consistent strumming energy through the fade
Final resolution on Em7 chord

guitar.pickup: Acoustic guitar or semi-hollow with P-90 pickups for the recorded tone

amp.recommended: Any clean acoustic amplifier or PA system

effects.reverb: Light room reverb for acoustic ambiance
effects.other: Capo on 2nd fret (essential). No effects pedals required - pure acoustic/clean tone.

beginner.focus: Learn the basic chord shapes with anchored fingers and the capo technique
steps: Get a capo and learn to place it correctly on the 2nd fret
Practice the Em7, G, Dsus4, and A7sus4 shapes with anchored ring and pinky fingers
Work on smooth transitions between the four main chords
Learn the basic down-strum rhythm before adding the full pattern

intermediate.focus: Master the strumming pattern and play through the complete song structure
steps: Learn the full Down-Down-Up-Up-Down-Up strumming pattern
Practice the pattern at 87 BPM with a metronome
Add the C chord for the pre-chorus section
Play through the entire song structure with correct timing

advanced.focus: Add dynamics, vocal accompaniment, and authentic tone nuances
steps: Add dynamic variation between verse (softer) and chorus (louder)
Practice singing while strumming the pattern
Experiment with slight strumming variations for expressiveness
Learn the lead guitar melody that appears in the outro

commonMistakes: Lifting the anchored ring and pinky fingers during chord changes
Rushing the strumming pattern - keep it steady at 87 BPM
Strumming too aggressively - Wonderwall has a flowing, relaxed feel
Placing the capo incorrectly, causing buzzing or sharp tuning
practiceRoutine: Warm up by practicing the anchored finger chord shapes for 5 minutes
Work on the strumming pattern on a single chord (Em7) for 3 minutes
Practice chord transitions: Em7 to G, G to Dsus4, Dsus4 to A7sus4
Play through the full verse progression at slow tempo, gradually increasing
Run through the entire song structure once at full tempo
focusAreas: Consistent strumming pattern with ghost strums
Smooth chord transitions without breaking rhythm
metronomeWork: Start at 60 BPM with just the strumming pattern on one chord
Increase by 5 BPM increments until reaching 87 BPM (song tempo)
Practice chord changes with metronome on beats 2 and 4 for feel
Use metronome to maintain steady tempo during full song play-through
